title: Reactivate brings a term back to Active and to the pickers
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, working in {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • COD is the shop's default for new customers.
  • Net 50 is deactivated.
  • Customer {Customer-A} holds COD.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S2-24 Customer.
  • Starting screen: the Credit Terms page (Settings, then "Credit Terms" in the Finance group) is open on the Inactive tab.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Click the "⋯" at the right of the "Net 50" row.
  2. Click "Reactivate".
  3. Click the "Active" tab.
  4. Open Edit Customer for {Customer-A} in a new tab.
  5. Open the Credit Terms dropdown.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the menu opens.
  • Step 2: no confirmation opens. Net 50 leaves the Inactive tab, both tab counts update, and a green toast shows "Net 50 reactivated".
  • Step 3: Net 50 is back on the Active tab between Net 45 and Net 60.
  • Step 4: Edit Customer opens.
  • Step 5: Net 50 is offered again, between Net 45 and Net 60.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11671 (Story 2, Row menu actions)

  • S2-R8: “"Reactivate" acts at once: the term moves back to the Active tab, the counts update, it appears in the customer and vendor pickers again, and a success toast shows "{name} reactivated".”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Term reactivated | "{name} reactivated" | Success toast”
  • Key Decisions: “Deactivating a term hides it from the customer and vendor pickers only. Everyone on it keeps it, shown as "{name} (Inactive)" on their card and in Edit, until someone picks another term; invoices print the plain name; it can be reactivated at any time.”
